newsitem.title: UK: World Bank plans euro Eurobond once cost-effective.
newsitem.headline: World Bank plans euro Eurobond once cost-effective.

text.p: The World Bank plans to launch a euro Eurobond once such an issue becomes cost-effective, a senior official told Reuters on Wednesday.

"We are looking for a funding opportunity and would be happy to (issue a euro Eurobond) as soon as it becomes cost-effective," Gumersindo Oliveros, senior manager of capital markets operations at the World Bank said.
"We are preparing ourselves for EMU and are closely monitoring developments. If it's cost-effective we would launch a (euro) bond tomorrow," said Oliveros, in London for a bond conference.
He said the World Bank was concerned about liquidity and whether or not a coupon would still be current when the euro is introduced.
Under plans for European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), the single currency is due to be introduced on January 1, 1999.

"We look for cost-effective funding and up to now the benchmark issue in euros, or in currencies that can be redenominated into euros, have really not been cost-effective for us relative to arbitrage opportunities in other markets," Oliveros said.
In January Austria launched the first bond with a clause allowing for its redenomination into euros once the single currency is introduced.
Other borrowers, like the European Investment Bank, L-Bank and Siemens, have followed. All launched bonds in a number of core EMU currencies like marks, French francs and guilders.
The deals will be fungible once the single currency is introduced, enhancing liquidity.
